title: Generalized Weakness
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with generalized weakness, fatigue, weight loss, fever, and flank pain. Classic triad of RCC: flank pain + palpable flank mass + hematuria. However, triad present only in 10% — most present with incidental finding or paraneoplastic syndromes. RCC is an adenocarcinoma of the renal cortex, most common type: clear cell carcinoma. Paraneoplastic syndromes: hypercalcemia (PTHrP), polycythemia (EPO), hypertension (renin), Stauffer syndrome (hepatic dysfunction without liver mets). Diagnosis: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast — enhancing renal mass. Renal US differentiates solid vs cystic. No biopsy needed before surgery if resectable. Treatment: localized → partial or radical nephrectomy. Metastatic → systemic therapy (immunotherapy — checkpoint inhibitors, targeted therapy — VEGF/TKI inhibitors). Cytoreductive nephrectomy in select metastatic patients. Refer urology/oncology.
chief_complaint: Generalized weakness, weight loss, flank pain, hematuria
